subject.title: fix(agents): exclude MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap

question: Should OpenClaw enforce the documented rule that shared channel sessions never receive MEMORY.md, even for deployments that currently rely on the undocumented behavior?
rationale: The patch closes a demonstrated cross-user context leak, but intentionally changes an existing runtime behavior for every shared channel and therefore needs explicit ownership of the security-versus-compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Enforce the documented boundary
options.body: Merge the channel-agnostic exclusion and treat shared-session MEMORY.md access as an unsafe undocumented behavior.

options.title: Require explicit migration messaging
options.body: Keep the fix but require focused upgrade/release-note context warning operators that shared channels will stop receiving MEMORY.md.

options.title: Preserve legacy behavior
options.body: Pause the PR and design an explicit opt-in compatibility policy, accepting that the unsafe behavior would remain available.

recommendation.title: Enforce the documented boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the channel-agnostic exclusion and treat shared-session MEMORY.md access as an unsafe undocumented behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The session classification and bootstrap history most strongly points to this owner for the cross-channel security boundary decision.
